name: battery-gauge
title: Battery gauge
summary: A battery icon filled to a host-supplied battery level (0-100) that turns red below 20%, with the percentage under it.
prompt: Make a battery widget that fills to the phone's battery percentage and turns red when it drops below 20%.
teaches: Take the level from an exported host float (resources.variables battery, default 76) and clamp it once into a local variable with clamp(0, 100, @battery)
Size the fill from it: right = 48 + 94 * @level / 100
Turn the fill red below 20% with conditionalOperations lt @level 20 around a paint change
Show "76%" as one centred text with textMerge of a textFromFloat and "%"

Fit a drawing authored at the header size to any box: a variable s = min(componentWidth() / W, componentHeight() / H), a translate by half the extra space and a scale by s about the design's centre; the background drawRect runs before it, to componentWidth() × componentHeight()

snippets.note: level = clamp(0, 100, @battery): the value goes last
the fill width follows the level

check.describe: Default: a green fill at 76% and "76%". variables {battery: 15}: a short red fill and "15%". Resized, the background fills the box and the battery scales to the shorter side, centred.

pitfalls: batteryLevel() (system variable 38) is an rcj/json2rc extension: the Java parser rejects it ("Unknown token in expression") and Android's RemoteContext defines no battery id, so a portable document takes the level from a host variable
clamp takes the value last: clamp(0, 100, @battery). clamp(@battery, 0, 100) returns 0 for any level
A conditionalOperations that only changes the paint must sit between the default paint and the draw: the red paint replaces the green one for the next drawRoundRect only when the test holds
textFromFloat pads to `whole` digits with a leading space (" 15"), which shifts centred text; flags 4 drops the padding

Canvas coordinates are pixels of the box the host gives the document, not of the header: a background drawRect to the literal header size leaves the rest of a bigger box unpainted, and literal positions get cut off in a smaller one
